item.title: Towada-Hachimantai National Park: Akita's Volcanic Highland — Guide
item.description: The Hachimantai plateau in northern Akita is a volcanic highland of crater lakes, alpine marshes and steaming vents. The Aspite Line mountain road (open May–November) traverses the plateau past five-colour marshes and the Hachimantai summit — one of Japan’s great scenic drives, turning incandescent gold and crimson in mid-October. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kazuno (Hachimantai), Akita Hours Aspite Line ~May–Nov, daytime Admission Free Time needed Half day Best time Mid-Oct (autumn); summer alpine What to See The scenic Aspite Line drive across the plateau.

item.title: Daisetsuzan National Park Guide: Hiking, Ropeway & Autumn
item.description: Daisetsuzan is the vast, wild roof of Hokkaido — the island’s largest national park, sometimes called “the playground of the gods” by the Ainu. A sprawling massif of volcanic peaks, alpine meadows, gorges and hot springs, it centres on Asahidake, Hokkaido’s highest mountain (2,291 m). A ropeway whisks visitors into the high country for easy boardwalk strolls or serious hikes, and each September the park lights up with Japan’s earliest autumn colours.

item.title: Shiretoko Peninsula Guide: UNESCO Nature, Cruises & Bears
item.description: Jutting into the Sea of Okhotsk at Hokkaido’s far northeast, the Shiretoko Peninsula is one of Japan’s last great wildernesses — a UNESCO World Heritage site where primeval forest, volcanic peaks and a wild coast of cliffs and waterfalls shelter an extraordinary density of wildlife. This is brown bear country, home also to deer, foxes, eagles and, offshore, whales and seals. Explore the Shiretoko Five Lakes, take a nature cruise beneath sea cliffs, and in late winter watch drift ice pack the shore.
